Parallel metadata reports actual parallel use, two subagents, finished state, artifact_ok and process_ok true, and 37/37 quality pass.
Current completed official evaluation reports solution_passed true with 37 passed of 37 evaluated testcases and protocol validation confirming AgentSwarm use.
Official Docker evaluator summary completed successfully with pass_rate 1.0 and solution_passed true.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream records the parallel session lifecycle, AgentSwarm launch, child completion events, parent rebuild/diff checks, and final completed prompt.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the workspace session directory used by the main and two child actors.

Implementation child receives the full porting task, writes Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/sortedcontainers.rs, test18.rs, builds with cargo and rustc, fixes negative overflow in atoi, and reports clean verification.
Probing child runs the C++ reference across required numeric and argument parsing cases, kills one huge-value probe after it hangs, reruns with timeout, and returns exact behavioral notes.

Parallel parent inspects the empty output and reference executable, delegates implementation and probing as separate child scopes, receives both completed results, rebuilds, diffs both binaries, and finalizes.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the required pure Rust 2021 port, exact stdout matching, std-only constraint, complete Cargo structure, root test18.rs, standalone rustc compatibility, tuple-key sorted map semantics, bool 0/1 formatting, operator[] insertion, update, bounds, equal_range, and atoi argument behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent first explored the environment, then launched two non-conflicting children: agent-0 owned implementation, build, and verification in /output, while agent-1 owned black-box probing only and was explicitly told not to modify files. Parent retained final review and acceptance.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 created Cargo.toml, src/sortedcontainers.rs, src/lib.rs, and test18.rs. It implemented SortedMap over BTreeMap with insert, contains, index/index_assign, keys/values, erase, find, lower_bound, upper_bound, equal_range, get, update, clear, size, and empty, then fixed negative overflow handling in atoi after a diff exposed it.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Because only agent-0 wrote deliverables and agent-1 only probed, integration consisted of adopting agent-0's shared /output files. The parent listed the final tree, rebuilt with cargo and rustc, and delivered the project layout and semantics summary.
parallel.verification: Agent-0 compared both rustc and cargo binaries against the reference over mandatory and extra cases, found and fixed a negative overflow mismatch, then reported all clean. Parent independently rebuilt and diffed default, numeric, weird argument, and extra argument cases and saw ALL_DIFFS_CLEAN.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task-relevant work is visible at closure. Agent-1 killed a deliberately huge positive reference probe and documented it as a hang, but that was a probing subprocess rather than required implementation output and did not leave final acceptance unverified.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same pure Rust 2021, exact-output, std-only, Cargo project, root test18.rs, black-box inference, and reference executable requirements, including tuple lexicographic order, operator[] default insertion, bool formatting, and atoi-like prefix parsing.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor owned the complete flow: environment check, reference probing, implementation, build, targeted behavioral comparisons, edge-case parsing checks, and final delivery. There was no delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/sorted_map.rs, and test18.rs. It implemented a generic SortedMap wrapper over BTreeMap and then edited test18.rs to replace Rust parse with a custom atoi that handles leading whitespace, signs, digit prefixes, and failure-to-zero behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All artifacts were produced by the same actor in /output, with src/lib.rs wiring the library and test18.rs as the package root entry. The final response reported the layout, fidelity details, and verification results.
serial.verification: Serial built with cargo release, diffed output for default, numeric, and negative cases, then checked argument parsing cases such as 18abc, leading-space 7, +5, and xyz, all of which matched the reference.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task-relevant work is visible at closure. The official evaluator completed and passed all 37 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel preserved the prompt obligations, including exact output, std-only code, Cargo structure, root test18.rs, and black-box verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and recognized the same obligations, including exact output and the need for atoi-style parsing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage gap is evidenced; both recognized and satisfied the tested obligations, with parallel probing more explicit about unusual C atoi overflow behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent used AgentSwarm with one implementation/verification child and one read-only probing child, then kept final acceptance ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for all implementation, testing, and delivery work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The process shape differed substantially, but ownership was clear in both: parallel implementation was owned by agent-0 and probing by agent-1, while serial had one owner for the whole flow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave agent-0 the source excerpt, key semantics, file layout, standalone rustc constraint, and mandatory verification list, while agent-1 received a read-only probing scope.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial held all task context locally and did not need handoff interfaces between actors.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No harmful context loss or interface conflict is visible; the parallel child brief contained the implementation contract and the probing result was returned before parent verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Agent-0 implemented a concrete BTreeMap-based SortedMap module and root test18.rs, then corrected the first atoi overflow implementation after a failing edge comparison.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a generic BTreeMap-based SortedMap module and root test18.rs, then corrected argument parsing from Rust parse to atoi-like prefix parsing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation paths converged on correct BTreeMap semantics and custom argument parsing. Parallel fixed a negative overflow edge found in its expanded tests; serial fixed stricter parsing before final checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both children completed and returned summaries to the parent; parent then performed its own build and diff checks after receiving the aggregate swarm result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to join; serial progressed locally from write to build to verification to final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a result lifecycle to manage and did so: child results were available, acknowledged, and followed by parent-side validation. Serial had no comparable coordination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only agent-0 wrote deliverables in /output while agent-1 was read-only. Parent later rebuilt the final tree containing Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/sortedcontainers.rs, test18, and test18.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same class of deliverables itself: Cargo.toml, test18.rs, src/lib.rs, src/sorted_map.rs, and release build artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used shared workspace side effects from one implementation child, but there was no competing writer or incompatible component merge; serial avoided shared-state coordination by being single actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified inside agent-0, corrected an overflow bug, verified again for both binaries, and the parent independently rebuilt and diffed required and extra cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built once, diffed required and representative edge cases, and closed after all checks passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more layered verification due to the implementation child, probing child, and parent checks. Serial had fewer checks but enough to pass the same official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel took longer and used two subagents, including time spent on a probing subprocess that hung until stopped, but closed with parent post-checks and no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished faster with no subagents, no delegation overhead, and no process timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget for broader probing, but the added time did not shorten closure or leave required work unfinished; both official runs completed well within the cell budget.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial passed all 37 testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is process shape, not outcome: parallel delegated implementation and black-box probing to two children and then parent-verified the shared output, while serial implemented and verified the same required behavior in one actor. No parallel coordination episode produced an adverse unresolved task result.
parallel_contributors: Agent-0 implemented the final project and fixed a negative overflow atoi bug after diffing edge cases.
Agent-1 provided independent reference behavior observations that the parent received before final verification.
The parent rebuilt and diffed the delivered artifacts after child completion.
serial_contributors: The single serial actor implemented the final project, replaced strict parsing with atoi-like parsing, and verified required and edge outputs.
The serial run avoided delegation overhead but did not solve a different task or rely on a different evaluator.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial originally started with Rust parse and then corrected it to custom atoi semantics.
Parallel agent-0 originally mishandled negative overflow saturation and then corrected it.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both current official evaluations passed

candidates.reason: Parallel explicitly assigned implementation and verification ownership to agent-0, and agent-0 wrote the final project files.
There were not multiple separately implemented components needing reconciliation; the sole writer produced a coherent project and the parent verified it.
Agent-0 wrote the required root entry file and Cargo project, and the parent rebuilt the final deliverable before closure.
The parent retained the end-to-end transition by receiving child results, rebuilding, testing, and issuing the final delivery summary.
The implementation child began and wrote files while the probing child was also active; productive work was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight.
Investigation did not complete as a separate first phase before implementation; the implementation and probing children overlapped, and implementation finished successfully.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; the implementation child completed, fixed the observed bug, and the parent had time for final verification.
Fan-out was limited to two children and did not exhaust the cell budget; both child results returned and parent closure included build and diff checks.
Agent-0's implementation task was broad but completed and checkpointed through files, builds, fixes, and clean verification; agent-1's probing hang was handled and not indispensable unfinished work.

The implementation child brief included the source, output identity requirement, std-only rule, Cargo/root-file layout, standalone rustc constraint, and verification cases; no known requirement omission caused unusable work.
Parallel did not assign interoperating components to separate writers; the only writer owned the complete project while the second child was read-only probing, so no cross-agent contract was missing.
No known finding disappeared in transfer; both child summaries reached the parent through the swarm result and the parent then used them for final checks.
The child reports were lengthy but decision-structured, and the parent reduced them to concrete final rebuild and diff actions rather than leaving dependent action unfinished.
No child result described a superseded workspace state that the parent consumed; parent rebuilt the current /output tree after receiving the child results.
The implementation and probing reports did not give incompatible contracts requiring adjudication; parent final checks confirmed the delivered behavior.
The parent did not accept completion solely from child claims; it rebuilt the current tree and ran final output diffs before final response.
There was no replacement or retry child repeating prior work without inherited findings; the only correction was an in-place edit by agent-0 using its own diff evidence.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: A probing subprocess was stopped after a huge reference input hung, but no child agent was terminated before needed task work or result finalization; both child agents completed.
A promotable project existed after agent-0 completed, and parent finalization began promptly with rebuild and diff checks; no complete candidate was left unpromoted before closure.
There was no post-verification merge of a child change; agent-0 fixed and verified first, then the parent ran post-handoff build and diff checks.
Agent-0's implementation was available in the shared output tree and the parent adopted it by listing, rebuilding, and testing those files before final delivery.
The probing child produced a concrete verifier-like report and it returned to the parent inside the AgentSwarm aggregate result before parent checks.
The only stopped work was a hanging reference probe inside agent-1, which the child itself stopped and reran with timeout; no required child failed without takeover.
The completed child reports were visible to the parent and were followed by parent-side build and diff checks rather than ignored inconsistent action.
Agent-1 waited on a known huge-input probe and then inspected output, stopped it, and reran with timeout; the parent did not blindly wait until the run deadline.
Parallel did not have competing implementation designs in different files; agent-0 was the only implementation writer and agent-1 only probed the reference binary.
No two live agents edited the same file; write events for Cargo.toml, src files, and test18.rs all came from agent-0 before parent verification.
The only source replacement was agent-0 editing its own test18.rs implementation after a diff; it did not overwrite another actor's source.
Parent later rebuilt the executable after child completion, but no live actor owned or used the deliverable concurrently and no conflicting entry-point replacement is proven.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs from another actor; the parent merely rebuilt and verified the completed tree.
Although the implementation child wrote in the shared /output workspace, there was no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem because no other live writer touched the implementation files.
No generated artifact from one actor was consumed by another as a false reference environment; all checks compared against the provided C++ reference binary and current Rust outputs.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Agent-1's huge-value reference probe temporarily ran in the background and was killed, but the same chain is rejected for Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Blind Timeout Wait, Oversized Child Task, and Fan-out Budget Exhaustion because it was a bounded probing subprocess, not unfinished required implementation or exhausted closure budget.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no parallel-side event had both a realized adverse process consequence and a task-solving contrast.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained because both runs passed and the observable parallel coordination differences were productive or harmless rather than adverse.
